scope: Filter occurrences in these illustrative Bentheimer examples; this is not scientific validation or complete plugin coverage.

filters.purpose: Create the native 75 cubed grid at 18 micrometer spacing. Both released cubes span 1350 micrometers per axis; use a common example-local corner origin.
Import exact author-normalized UInt16 little-endian bytes as one scalar per cell. Inherit tuple dimensions from CellData; no byte header, normalization, cropping, or axis permutation is applied.
Create the native 225 cubed grid at 6 micrometer spacing. Both released cubes span 1350 micrometers per axis; use a common example-local corner origin.
Import exact author-normalized UInt16 little-endian bytes as one scalar per cell. Inherit tuple dimensions from CellData; no byte header, normalization, cropping, or axis permutation is applied.

Express the author-normalized intensity on a shared Float32 scale using the fixed paper display maximum 20000. Preserve values above one; this is neither per-volume min-max normalization nor a probability.

Express the author-normalized intensity on a shared Float32 scale using the fixed paper display maximum 20000. Preserve values above one; this is neither per-volume min-max normalization nor a probability.

Replicate each 18 micrometer cell onto an exact 225 cubed, 6 micrometer grid. Retain the native geometry. This nearest-neighbor mapping adds no measured detail and does not reproduce cubic interpolation or EDSR.

Compute absolute Float32 differences between matching cells of the mapped 18 micrometer scan and the measured 6 micrometer scan. Equal grid dimensions, spacing and origins must be established before interpreting this as spatial discrepancy.
Compute count, minimum, maximum and mean over every common-grid cell. These are intensity summaries, not porosity, permeability, or accuracy scores.

Set the explicit lower-corner origin to (-675,-675,-675) micrometers without changing spacing or data. This centers the example-local 1350 micrometer field of view; it does not recover scanner coordinates.
